title: Permutations
statement: You get a list of different integers. Return every way to put all of them in a row: each number appears exactly once in each arrangement, and different orders count as different answers. The arrangements can come back in any order.

example.caption: Three numbers can be lined up in 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 different orders.

idea.sentence: Fill the slots one by one. For each slot, try every number that is not already used, then free it again when you back up.

jargon.plain: Make a choice, explore everything that follows, then undo the choice and try the next one.
An arrangement of all the items where order matters: [1,2] and [2,1] are two permutations.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of different numbers, e.g. [1,2,3] (keep it to 3 or 4)

compare.bruteLabel: Try every n-length sequence, drop repeats
compare.unit: paths looked at (rough). The true count is n! which grows faster than 2^n

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Fill every slot with any of the n numbers, then throw away sequences that repeat a number. Most are thrown away.

rows.name: Backtracking with used[]
rows.note: There are n! orders and each copy costs n. The used flags stop a number from appearing twice, so no dead sequences are built.

fast.takeaway: n! is the size of the answer, so the work cannot shrink. The used flags make sure none of it is wasted.

stages.title: Start empty
stages.note: path is the order so far. used[i] says whether nums[i] is already in it.

stages.title: Choose
stages.note: Mark nums[i] used, push it on the path, and fill the next slot.

stages.title: Skip used
stages.note: A number already in the path cannot appear twice. Skip it.

stages.title: Record
stages.note: When the path is as long as nums, every slot is filled. Save a copy.

stages.title: Undo
stages.note: Pop the number and clear its used flag so the next branch can use it. Return all results at the end.

edges.title: One number
edges.why: One slot and one number. There is only one way to line it up.

edges.title: Order matters
edges.why: Unlike subsets, [0,1] and [1,0] are different answers.

edges.title: Negatives
edges.why: The search uses positions, not values, so negative numbers and zero need no special case.

edges.title: Factorial growth
edges.why: Each extra number multiplies the count by the new length. Keep presets to 3 or 4 numbers.

gotchas.text: Push [...path], not path. The array is popped later, so a stored reference would end up empty.
Save append([]int{}, path...). Appending path itself shares one backing array, and every saved permutation would be overwritten by the next ones.
Clear used[i] right after the pop. If you forget, later branches see numbers as taken and results go missing.
Use a used array indexed by position, not path.includes(x), for speed. includes scans the path on every try.
The result order is up to you. The test driver sorts it, because the order inside each permutation is what counts, and sorting inside would hide errors.

recap.key: Fill slot by slot. Try each unused number, mark it, recurse, then unmark. Save a copy when the path is full.
recap.complexity: Time O(n · n!). Space O(n) for the recursion, plus the output.
moves: Pop and unmark to backtrack; save a copy at full length
